strings.title: Dividing with the Area Model
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Divide a three-digit number by a two-digit number with the area model: take out 10 groups first, then see what's left.
strings.keywords: divide, area model, 10 groups, how many groups, quotient, what's left
watchFor: Splitting by place value (156 = 100 + 50 + 6) when those parts don't divide by 12: ask "How much is 10 groups of 12? Start there."
Forgetting to add the parts of the quotient: ask "How many 12s altogether?"
Losing track of what's left: ask "What's 156 − 120?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why did we always start with 10 groups?" Land: 10 times the divisor is easy, so take it out first; then divide what's left and add the parts. The area model shows the side lengths adding up.

problems.notes: Look for: 10 × 12 = 120, 24 left is 2 × 12. Ask: "How many 12s?" Word choice: "how many groups of 12". Model: area 144 / 12 = 120 + 24

responses.say: 10 twelves is 120, 24 left is 2 more twelves. 12.
responses.tip: The target strategy.
A fact. Ask: how could you check it?

problems.notes: Look for: 120 + 36. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: area 156 / 12 = 120 + 36

responses.say: 144 is 12 twelves, plus one more 12 is 156. 13.
responses.tip: Used the last problem.
Forgot the 10 groups in 120. Ask: how many 12s are in 120?

problems.notes: Look for: 140 + 28. Ask: "What's 10 groups of 14?" Model: area 168 / 14 = 140 + 28

responses.tip: Halving both numbers. Ask: why is the answer the same?

problems.notes: Look for: 150 + 45. Ask: "How many 15s in 45?" Model: area 195 / 15 = 150 + 45

responses.say: 200 is 13 fifteens and 5 more, so 195 is 13.

responses.tip: Stopped after 10 groups. Ask: can 45 make more 15s?

problems.notes: Look for: 240 + 48. Ask: "Is there a bigger first chunk?" Model: area 288 / 24 = 240 + 48

responses.tip: Ask: why can we halve both?

problems.notes: Look for: 210 + 42. Ask: "What's the same as 288 ÷ 24?" Model: area 252 / 21 = 210 + 42
Look for: 250 + 50, or 4 quarters in each 100. Ask: "How is this like money?" Model: area 300 / 25 = 250 + 50

responses.tip: Like quarters in dollars.

strings.title: What Do We Do with the Remainder?
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: The same division can have different answers depending on the story: round up (buses), drop the leftover (full pages), or share it as a fraction (ribbon).
strings.keywords: remainder, round up, left over, context, fraction, makes sense
watchFor: Giving 8 1/3 buses: ask "Can we order a third of a bus?"
Always rounding up or always dropping the remainder: ask "What does the leftover mean in this story?"
Losing the remainder entirely: ask "How many are left after the full groups?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why did 100 ÷ 12 have three different answers?" Land: the division is the same, but the story decides: buses round up to 9, full pages drop the leftover (8), and ribbon shares it as a fraction (8 1/3).

problems.notes: Context: "96 students, 12 on each bus." Look for: 8 × 12 = 96. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: ratio buses:students, 1:12, 8:96

Context: "100 students, 12 on each bus. How many buses?" Look for: 8 full buses, 4 students left: 9 buses. Ask: "Does 8 1/3 buses make sense?" Model: text 100 = 96 + 4 ; 8 buses full, 4 students left ; 9 buses

responses.say: 8 buses are full and 4 students are left, so we need 9 buses.
responses.tip: Round up: everyone needs a seat.
The math is right. Ask: can we order a third of a bus?

problems.notes: Context: "100 stickers, 12 on each page. How many full pages?" Look for: 8 full pages, 4 stickers left over. Ask: "What's different from the buses?" Model: text 100 = 96 + 4 ; 8 full pages, 4 stickers left

responses.say: 8 full pages, with 4 stickers left over.
responses.tip: Drop the leftover: it isn't a full page.
Rounded up like the buses. Ask: is the 9th page full?

problems.notes: Context: "100 cm of ribbon cut into 12 equal pieces. How long is each piece?" Look for: 8 1/3 cm. Ask: "Can the leftover be shared this time?" Model: text 100 = 96 + 4 ; 4 ÷ 12 = 4/12 = 1/3 ; 8 1/3 cm

responses.say: 8 cm each, and the 4 cm left shared by 12 is 1/3 cm more.
responses.tip: Share the leftover as a fraction.
Ask: what happens to the last 4 cm of ribbon?

problems.notes: Context: "150 muffins, boxes hold 12. How many boxes do we need?" Look for: 12 full boxes, 6 left: 13 boxes. Ask: "Round up or drop it?" Model: area 144 / 12 = 120 + 24

responses.say: 12 boxes is 144, 6 muffins left, so 13 boxes.
responses.tip: Ask: why 13 and not 12 1/2?
Dropped the leftover. Ask: where do the last 6 muffins go?

problems.notes: Context: "250 hours. How many full days is that?" Look for: 10 full days (240 h), 10 hours left. Ask: "Which kind of remainder is this?" Model: text 250 = 240 + 10 ; 240 ÷ 24 = 10 ; 10 days and 10 hours

responses.tip: Drop the leftover, or name it in hours.

strings.title: Dividing in Friendly Chunks
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Divide by a two-digit number by taking out friendly chunks: 20 groups, 10 groups, 1 group. The area model shows the chunks side by side.
strings.keywords: divide, area model, chunks, 10 groups, 20 groups, quotient
watchFor: Taking out only 10 groups when 20 fit: ask "Could you take a bigger chunk?"
Losing track of the chunks: ask "How many groups altogether?"
Splitting 276 into 200 + 76: ask "Does 200 share evenly by 12?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did you choose your chunks?" Land: use friendly multiples of the divisor: 10, 20 or 25 groups, then what's left. Add the chunks for the answer.

problems.notes: Look for: 20 × 12 = 240. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: text 12 x 20 = 240
Look for: 240 + 12: 20 + 1. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Word choice: "chunks". Model: area 252 / 12 = 240 + 12

responses.tip: The target strategy.
Ask: is 12 × 2 close to 252?

problems.notes: Look for: 240 + 36: 20 + 3. Ask: "What's left after 20 groups?" Model: area 276 / 12 = 240 + 36
Look for: 250 + 75: 10 + 3. Or think quarters: $3.25 is 13 quarters. Ask: "How is this like money?" Model: area 325 / 25 = 250 + 75

responses.tip: Money connection.

problems.notes: Look for: 360 + 18: 20 + 1. Ask: "What's 20 groups of 18?" Model: area 378 / 18 = 360 + 18

responses.tip: Ask: is 18 × 12 close to 378? What's 18 × 20?

problems.notes: Look for: 320 + 96: 10 + 3. Ask: "How many 32s in 96?" Model: area 416 / 32 = 320 + 96
Look for: 500 + 125: 20 + 5. Ask: "Quarters again?" Model: area 625 / 25 = 500 + 125
